terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō): with an accusative, often with ad sē
evidence: Cic. Div. 1.86: magnētem lapidem … quī ferrum ad sē adliciat et attrahat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a magnet drawing iron, and of whatever draws people: money, rewards, kindness, success. Often “entice”, in a bad sense. Frequent in Cicero, never in Terence, Horace or Juvenal (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with an accusative
terms.comment: Physical drawing and dragging, of a magnet or of a person brought by force (tribūnōs attrahī ad sē jussit, Liv. 29.9, Lewis & Short); figuratively, drawing someone to a place or a cause.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: the person or thing gained in the accusative, the person won over to in the dative
evidence: Liv. 4.48.9: prīmōribus sē patrum concilient (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Attract in the sense of winning goodwill. Its first sense is “bring together, unite” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: magnētem lapidem … quī ferrum ad sē adliciat et attrahat
phrases.english: the magnet stone, which draws and pulls iron to itself
the success of the wicked lures more people on

phrases.latin: Cōmis enim et blanda salūtātiō saepe conciliat amīcitiam, inimīcitiam dīluit
phrases.english: a friendly and pleasant greeting often wins friendship and washes away enmity
phrases.source: Erasm. Coll., Fōrm., In prīmō congressū, I 3

sources: Lewis & Short: allicio · Lewis & Short: attraho · Lewis & Short: concilio
